description: Target the serial-batch launch-overhead bottleneck on small n (32,176,352): custom CUDA C++ unblocked Householder QR, one matrix per threadblock, grid-strided over the batch so all matrices run concurrently. Stage in shared memory where it fits, register/global tiling above ~n=200 (B200 228KB/SM can't hold 352^2 fp32). Emit compact (H,tau) in exact geqrf convention: v below diagonal with implicit unit diagonal, R in triu, signed-beta=-sign(x0)||x||, tau=0 on zero/near-zero pivots (rankdef). Route any n not in {32,176,352,512,1024,2048,4096} to torch.geqrf.

Target compute throughput + serial-batch on large n (512,1024,2048,4096): all-custom CUDA C++ blocked (panel) Householder QR with custom kernels for panel factorization, T-matrix (larft) and block-reflector trailing update (larfb), grid-strided over the batch so arbitrary B (96,160,640,1280) runs concurrently, fp32. Emit compact (H,tau) in exact geqrf convention. Handle rankdef exact-zero pivots (tau=0, identity reflector) and nearrank/clustered cancellation via signed-beta safe-scaling; hold the tight orthogonality gate. Route off-grid n to torch.geqrf.

Target the FLOP-heavy trailing update on batched n=512/1024 by exploiting the ~2400x accuracy slack: blocked Householder where larfb/larft run as cuBLAS/CUTLASS strided-batched GEMM in tf32 tensor-core math mode (fp32 accumulate), with only panel factorization a custom CUDA C++ kernel. Keep Householder vectors/tau fp32 for the compact (H,tau) contract. Verify ill-conditioned (nearrank/clustered/mixed) hold the orthogonality gate (tf32 not raw bf16); route off-grid n to torch.geqrf.

Combine the three round-1 branches into one best-per-shape n-dispatch kernel. Base on W2 (5ac6f2c0, global best 14857us: custom n in {176,352,512,1024}). Graft W0's faster small-n kernels (7f74c295: n=32 55us, n=176 588us, n=352 2518us) and W1's n=2048 custom path (961505a: 1.56x over geqrf). Pick the measured-fastest kernel per n; geomean weights every shape equally so upgrading n=32/176/352/2048 off geqrf is as valuable as the dominant n=512. Resolve kernel-name/load_inline/shared-mem conflicts when merging the three CUDA sources. Keep exact (H,tau), off-grid-n->geqrf, hold all guards. Should beat 14857us and become the new global best.

Push the dominant n=512/1024 shapes past the global best (5ac6f2c0): ~17% of n=512 time is V-construction (tril+eye) + the per-panel larft Python loop. Emit the unit-lower V and the T-matrix DIRECTLY from the custom panel kernel (you prototyped emit-V race-free; in-kernel larft was buggy - get it correct this time), eliminating the host-side tril/eye and the larft loop so the trailing update consumes kernel outputs directly. fp32 (tf32 confirmed no help, breaks the n=512 gate). Keep exact (H,tau), off-grid-n->geqrf, hold ill-conditioned gates.

Crack the severely under-occupied low-batch tall shapes n=2048 (B=8, 74ms) and n=4096 (B=2, 50ms) - the two largest geomean terms, currently routed to slow geqrf because one-block-per-matrix and batched-GEMM both collapse when matrices<188 SMs. First measure a per-matrix path: loop the small batch calling a single-matrix blocked QR where one large n x n factorization + its trailing GEMM saturates all 188 SMs on its own (try explicit cusolverDnSgeqrf, torch.linalg.qr, vs a custom multi-block-per-matrix kernel with global sync between panels via kernel-relaunch or grid.sync, whichever benchmarks faster). Only keep what beats geqrf. Keep small-n paths, exact (H,tau), off-grid-n->geqrf, hold ill-conditioned gates. (CAQR/TSQR is wrong for square matrices.)

Re-combine onto W2's emit-VT base (0a60aa5d, 9660us: faster n=352=1834us, n=512=18700us, n=1024=15530us than the prior combine's components). Graft W0's small-n kernels (7f74c295: n=32=55, n=176=589) and W1's n=2048 custom path (961505a, 1.56x over geqrf), keeping n=4096+offgrid->geqrf. Re-measure each n on this base and pick the measured-fastest per shape (e.g. n=176/352 may now be W2's emit-VT, not W0 - verify). Keep 3 separate load_inline modules to avoid panel_factor symbol clashes. Exact (H,tau), all guards. Target a new global best below 9000us.

Cut the n=512 (4/12 shapes, ~18.7ms) and n=1024 trailing-update DRAM traffic, which is memory-bound because rank-nb<=32 skinny bmms make many passes over A2. Restructure to a WIDER WY outer block (NB~64-128): factor the wide panel with your emit-VT inner kernel in nb<=32 sub-steps, accumulate the inner T-blocks into ONE outer compact-WY (V,T) over NB columns, then apply the trailing update as ONE larger rank-NB fp32 bmm per outer block (higher arithmetic intensity, fewer A2 passes). Stay fp32 (tf32 confirmed to break the n=512 gate). Exact (H,tau), off-grid->geqrf, hold rankdef/clustered/nearrank/mixed gates.

High-risk/high-reward on dominant n=512 (4/12 shapes): the fp32 trailing GEMM is ~5% of peak. Run the FLOP-heavy trailing-update GEMM in bf16/fp16 on tensor cores (fp32 accumulate) then RESTORE fp32 accuracy by iterative refinement on the factorization (one Householder/QR correction sweep, or block-Newton on the WY update residual) so the final compact (H,tau) still passes factor rtol=20*n*eps and orth rtol=100*n*eps. The structural challenge: ill-conditioned columns (rankdef zero-pivot, clustered eps-scaled, nearrank) without conditioning dispatch (invariance guard) - handle low-precision breakdown by a per-column/per-block STRUCTURAL fallback to fp32, not a batch-level conditioning test. Use your verified V-build/larft kernels. If reduced-precision cannot hold the gate after refinement, log the negative cleanly and revert. Exact (H,tau), off-grid->geqrf.

Now that two-level blocking cut the trailing GEMM to ~33%, the PANEL KERNEL geqr2_vt is the dominant cost (53% of n=512, 49% of n=1024). Restructure it: (a) FUSE the in-kernel Gram (G=V^T V, ~33% of geqr2_vt) into the column-by-column factorization so reflector dot products are computed once and reused for larft instead of recomputed in a separate pass; (b) register-tile the warp-per-column factorization and use a better (warp-shuffle tree) reduction to cut the serial dot chain; (c) remove redundant per-step __syncthreads. Profile geqr2_vt with ncu to target the actual stall reason (likely barrier/MIO). Keep nb<=32 emit-VT correctness, exact (H,tau), off-grid->geqrf, hold all ill-conditioned gates. Target n=512 below 16ms.

Raise geqr2_vt occupancy on n=512/1024 (the panel kernel is 52%/49% of GPU time). Root issue is LAUNCH GRANULARITY, not matrix count: at n=512 B=640 there are 3.4 matrices/SM but each block is one fat warp grinding 512 rows column-by-column with a big smem panel, so blocks/SM is latency-starved. Attack the grid/occupancy shape ONLY: shrink per-block smem footprint and/or assign fewer warps per matrix with many more matrices concurrently in flight, so the 640 matrices saturate 188 SMs with latency-hiding slack. Use ncu occupancy/blocks-per-SM to drive it. CONSTRAINT: treat the per-matrix column-loop factorization body as a black box - do NOT rewrite the warp-per-column reduction or register tiling (another worker owns that). fp32, exact (H,tau), off-grid->geqrf, hold ill-conditioned gates.

Eliminate non-kernel overhead around the emit-VT path on n=512/1024. (1) The two-level path still runs a host-side per-panel Python loop forming T (T[:, :j, j] = bmm(T[:,:j,:j], z) over nb columns) - replace it with one batched/vectorized op or fold it into the existing in-kernel larft so there's no Python column loop. (2) The standalone H-clone memcpy is ~10%/5% of n=512/1024 (the benchmark reuses input across timed repeats so the original A must survive) - don't drop it blindly, but fold the copy into the kernel's ingest (read A, write working copy to scratch) or reuse a persistent preallocated scratch buffer so the separate memory-bound copy launch disappears. CONSTRAINT: do NOT change the in-kernel single-warp larft recurrence shape or nb<=32 (another worker owns the panel kernel internals). fp32, exact (H,tau), off-grid->geqrf, hold all gates.

Treat the emit-VT panel kernel as a FROZEN black box (W0/W2 own its grid + internals); own the trailing-update and cross-shape orchestration. (1) First profile per-shape gap and pick the least-polished shapes - geomean weights all 12 equally in log space, so cheap points live where we're furthest from optimal, not in the n=512 kernel two workers already attack. (2) Attack n=2048 (~32ms, the single biggest absolute-time custom shape, far from any vendor floor): it's plausibly trailing-GEMM-bound - try cuBLAS GEMM algo/layout selection, splitting the rank-NB trailing update, better-shaped bmm, or per-batch-slice overlap on the default stream. (3) Reduce small-n (n<=352) launch/host overhead. fp32, exact (H,tau), off-grid->geqrf, hold all gates. Do NOT edit the panel kernel column loop, Gram/larft, or its launch shape (collides with W0/W2).

Own per-shape two-level structure tuning (inner nb + outer NB co-selection) for the mid-n band, leading with n=1024 (currently nb=22/NB=88, 49% panel / 43% trailing - a different balance than n=512's 55/32). The inner/outer split is presently dictated by smem-fit, NOT co-optimized for each shape's panel/trailing balance: sweep and restructure inner-nb vs outer-NB (and the number of inner sub-steps per outer block) to minimize n=1024's total, then n=2048's two-level params. This is panel-internals/blocking-structure work, your strength via the fused-larft kernel. STAY OFF: the panel-kernel grid/occupancy/warps-per-matrix launch shape (W0 owns it, just hit 7569us there) and the trailing-GEMM/small-n orchestration (W1 owns it). Do NOT re-attempt the cross-warp-combine reduction (races at B>=640, you confirmed 4x) or tf32/fp16 (twice-failed). fp32, exact (H,tau), off-grid->geqrf, hold all gates.

Fill the GRID-STARVED large shapes n=1024 (B=60) and n=2048 (B=8) where matrices < 188 SMs, so one-block-per-matrix leaves most SMs idle (your occupancy lever maxed at 33% there). Build a MULTI-BLOCK-PER-MATRIX path: split ONE matrix's panel factorization + trailing update across multiple thread blocks (cooperative-groups grid.sync between panels, OR a multi-kernel design using kernel-relaunch as the global barrier - try both, pick faster), so a single large factorization saturates all 188 SMs. This is the algorithm change you flagged as outside your launch-shape lane - now in scope. Gut-check cheaply FIRST: confirm a multi-block trailing update + panel beats the current 7569us per-shape on n=1024/2048 before the full grid.sync rewrite; if it can't clear the vendor/one-block floor, log the clean negative and revert. Beware the sm_120 cross-warp-combine race W2 hit (B>=640): use single-warp or global-atomic/2-pass reductions across blocks. fp32, exact (H,tau), off-grid->geqrf, hold all gates.

Halve the panel kernel's shared-memory footprint to reach 2 blocks/SM. W0 proved geqr2_vt is smem-bound to 1 block/SM (the m*nb staged panel = ~64-75KB ⇒ Block-Limit-Shared-Mem=1, occ capped 33%), and that shrinking nb to fit 2 blocks is net-slower (trailing-GEMM loss). The body-level fix only you can do: now that you FUSED larft into the factor loop (brief 3), the separate Gram buffer sG is DEAD — overlap/alias it with sT (and any other now-unused staging) so per-block smem drops below ~50KB WITHOUT shrinking nb, letting 2 blocks/SM co-reside and roughly doubling occupancy again on n=512/1024/2048. Verify with ncu that blocks/SM goes to 2 and achieved occupancy rises. STAY OFF W0's launch-shape/nt grid lever and W1's trailing-GEMM/small-n. Don't touch the cross-warp reduction (races B>=640) or tf32/fp16 (settled negatives). fp32, exact (H,tau), off-grid->geqrf, hold all gates.

Consolidate the three scattered winning lineages into one best-per-shape kernel - none currently has all the wins. Stack: W2's 8e1568ca (CRACKED n=2048 two-level beats geqrf 2.35x=31.6ms + n=512 retune nb=24/NB=96), W0's 96792ec0 (nt=512 panel occupancy: 16.7->33.3%, NOT in W2's lineage), and your own f76d913c (adaptive panel width: grow nb as m shrinks, n=2048 +3.45%/n=1024 +2.93%). These compose: W0's launch-shape (nt), W2's per-shape nb/NB + n=2048 route, your adaptive-nb are largely independent layers of the same emit-VT kernel. Re-measure each n and verify the stacked kernel keeps every per-shape best; resolve any nt/nb interaction (W0's nt=512 assumed nb=32; W2 uses nb=24 at n=512 - re-tune nt for the new nb). Route n=2048 to the two-level custom path now (NOT geqrf), keep n=4096+offgrid->geqrf. Exact (H,tau), all guards. Target well below 7,550us global best.

Attack the small-n shapes n=176 (B=40, ~588us) and n=352 (B=40, ~1834us), frozen since round-1 and now the LEAST-polished non-vendor shapes - geomean weights all 12 equally in log space, so each is a full shape worth as much as n=512. These are GRID-UNDER-occupied (opposite of n=512): B=40 < 188 SMs, so one-block-per-matrix idles most SMs. Apply your occupancy expertise the other direction: pack MULTIPLE small matrices per block (n=176/352 panels are tiny in smem) so all 188 SMs fill, or 2D-tile so each SM holds several matrices concurrently. n=32 (B=20) is at the irreducible ~45us 2-launch-latency floor per W1 - leave it. This is fully orthogonal to W1's combine (n>=512) and W2's panel-internals/smem work. Profiling works now (bisect.py fix). fp32, exact (H,tau), off-grid->geqrf, hold all gates. Target n=176/352 meaningfully below 588/1834us.

BREAK THE fp32 PLATEAU (7550us is ~5x off the ~1300us leaderboard frontier, which uses low precision). Build a low-precision tensor-core trailing update for n=512/1024/2048. KEY INSIGHT: orthogonality is structurally free (checker rebuilds Q from your EMITTED fp32 (H,tau)), so only the factor residual via emitted R is at risk. The prior bf16 negative was bf16x1 - ONE LIMB SHORT. Use bf16x2 limbs (split each fp32 into hi+lo bf16, ~16 mantissa bits, error ~1.5e-5 = 25x UNDER the n=512 gate 6.1e-4, data-independent so NO conditioning dispatch). PRECISION MAP: panel factor fp32; V stored fp32 master + bf16x2 copy; tau fp32; T fp32-formed, bf16x2-applied; trailing A2 fp32 in global, convert to bf16x2 ONCE per wide outer step, do the 3 tensor-core GEMMs (hi.hi, hi.lo, lo.hi) with FP32 ACCUMULATE; emitted R (triu) ALWAYS fp32 written from fp32-accumulated A2. The 4-5x needs low-precision AND WIDE BLOCKS together: nb=128 (recursive 2x64->2x32 panel, inner reduction width<=32 = one warp to avoid the B>=640 race) makes the trailing GEMM compute-bound so tensor cores dominate. STAGE: (1) bf16x2 trailing at nb=32 FIRST, confirm n=512 mixed passes (cheap accuracy isolation); if it fails go bf16x3 (6 GEMMs, ~fp32); if bf16x3 fails too, log the clean negative (low-precision can't hold the gate). (2) then widen nb + recursive panel for speed. fp32 fallback for off-grid/small n. exact (H,tau), all guards. Target 1300-1700us.

Pursue YOUR OWN flagged lever: matrix-per-warp-group for the grid-starved n=352 (B=40, panel is 71% of time, 148 idle SMs). Rewrite the geqr2_vt panel path so each WARP-GROUP within a block factors a DIFFERENT matrix's panel as an independent warp-synchronous lane with NO cross-group __syncthreads - packing 2-4 small matrices per block WITHOUT the shared-sync serialization that killed naive matrices-per-block (brief 5), so the idle SMs get used. This is the fp32 panel-body rewrite you scoped; W2 has LEFT the fp32 panel kernel for the bf16 frontier so the fp32 body is yours now. Target n=352 (and n=176 if it transfers). Keep each matrix's factorization correct + race-free (warp-synchronous within a group, no cross-group shared combine - sidesteps the B>=640 race). This is orthogonal to W2 (bf16x2 trailing on n=512/1024/2048) and W1 (combine). fp32, exact (H,tau), off-grid->geqrf, hold all gates. If warp-group packing can't beat the current single-block-per-matrix n=352, log the clean negative.

Reach 2 blocks/SM on the n=1024/2048 panel by shrinking the STAGED smem in fp32 (NOT precision - bf16x2 is same 4 bytes as fp32, no saving; bf16x1 fails the gate). The panel is occupancy-limited because it stages the full m x nb panel (88/98KB at m=1024/2048 >> 50KB 2-block budget). TILE THE m-DIMENSION: the Householder reflector recurrence needs only the nb active columns + the nb x nb T-block in smem at once - stream the tall m-part from global in tile_m chunks (or hold it in registers), so staged smem = tile_m*nb instead of m*nb. That drops below the 50KB 2-block budget WITHOUT precision loss, unlocking the 2 blocks/SM fp32 'couldn't' reach on n=1024/2048 (you proved the full-panel version can't fit). Verify with ncu that blocks/SM goes 1->2 and achieved occupancy rises; keep the emit-VT (V + in-kernel larft) correctness. STAY OFF W0's launch-shape nt and the small-n shapes. Don't re-attempt bf16 panel/trailing (both settled negatives) or the cross-warp race. fp32, exact (H,tau), off-grid->geqrf, hold all gates.

Profile the NEW 6746us global best end-to-end and attack whatever is now the largest non-panel cost, staying out of the panel kernel (W0 owns its small-n warp-group body, W2 owns its m-tiling/occupancy). Re-measure the full per-shape + per-kernel breakdown on 6d52d834 (panel internals are off-limits, but everything else is yours): (1) the 3-separate-load_inline-module structure - does cross-module dispatch / redundant H allocation / the n-routing add measurable overhead now that per-shape kernels are fast? (2) n=512 trailing update is ~32-46% and fp32 - is the V^T A2 / T^T(...) / V@W sequence optimally shaped (fused baddbmm, layout, a single larger bmm vs two), independent of the panel? (3) is there cross-shape batching (e.g. running n=176 and n=352 panels concurrently, or overlapping the geqrf n=4096/n=32 path with custom-kernel shapes) that fills idle time? Find the biggest lever OUTSIDE the panel and pursue it. fp32, exact (H,tau), off-grid->geqrf, hold all gates.

Revisit bf16x2 trailing update but at WIDE nb to flip it compute-bound. Your earlier bf16 trailing negative was at rank-nb<=32 (memory-bound: 1.8-2.6x TC speedup lost to conversion traffic, net 0.38x). The fix: your two-level path ALREADY forms a wide outer block (NB=96/128) compact-WY (V,T) - apply the OUTER-block trailing update A2 -= V(T^T(V^T A2)) as bf16x2 tensor-core GEMMs at rank-NB>=64-128, where the (n x n x NB) GEMM is COMPUTE-bound and bf16 finally pays ~5x, while bf16x2 limbs hold the factor gate (you proved 9e-6 relerr, n512 mixed=0.24 vs gate 20). Keep the nb<=32 panel inner step + emitted (H,tau) in fp32 (only the wide outer trailing GEMM goes bf16x2). FIRST profile the panel-vs-trailing split on n=512/1024/2048: if the outer trailing update is a big enough share to matter, pursue it; if trailing is <20% of wall, log that the ceiling is panel-bound and stop. STAY OFF the panel internals (W0) and the fp32 orchestration/module/overlap lane (W1). exact (H,tau), off-grid->geqrf, hold all gates incl clustered/rankdef/mixed.

Harden the global best (6d52d834) for leaderboard robustness, since the secret ranked set uses shapes the public benchmark omits and a hidden bug there would void the submission. You wrote the off-grid-robustness guard, so you know the failure modes best. Stress the current best EXHAUSTIVELY beyond the 12 public shapes: every off-grid n (n%8!=0, n<32, the 352-512 gap, n>4096) routes to geqrf without fault/cascade; odd/large batches (B=1,3,96,160,1280) and the mixed/rankdef/clustered/nearrank/nearcollinear cases at the n the custom path handles; n exactly at the routing boundaries (511/513/1023/1025). Find any shape where the combined kernel faults, races (run compute-sanitizer at B>=640), or breaks a gate, and FIX the routing/kernel so the submission is secret-set-safe. If everything already holds, that is a valuable PASS result - log it with the evidence. This is orthogonal to W1 (fp32 orchestration) and W2 (bf16 trailing). Keep the 6746us geomean (don't regress the public shapes). exact (H,tau), hold all guards.

The ONE untried in-domain panel lever: N1 proved geqr2_vt is barrier/latency-bound but never DECOMPOSED what the barriers are spent on. Profile (ncu, from a non-/tmp dir) and split the panel's stall/sync time across {single-warp-per-column dots, in-kernel larft T-construction, column rank-1 updates}. If in-kernel larft T-build is a non-trivial share of the critical __syncthreads path, restructure it to cut/overlap syncs (e.g. overlap the T-column recurrence with the next reflector's dot, defer partial-T to the trailing-prep, or reduce the per-T-column barrier count) WITHOUT changing nb<=32 or the emit-VT correctness. MEASUREMENT-GATED: if larft T-build is <~10% of panel time, the fp32 panel is confirmed at its floor - log that clean finding and STOP (don't force a change). This is the last fp32 optimization probe; worth at most low-double-digit %. STAY OFF W0 (robustness hardening) and W1 (verification). fp32, exact (H,tau), off-grid->geqrf, hold all gates.

Verify the global best e889bbe8 as the submission candidate (we're at the local fp32 ceiling; correctness/reproducibility now matters more than more speed). Run the full benchmark 3+ times to confirm 6711us is STABLE not noise (report variance/error bars per shape); run validate incl all 3 guards and record the exact gate MARGINS per shape (factor residual vs 20*n*eps, orthogonality vs 100*n*eps) on every public + ill-conditioned case, so we know how much headroom exists before any B200 eps/timing difference could flip a gate. Flag any shape whose margin is thin (<2x). If you find a correctness or stability problem, fix it (that's a real win); if everything is solid, log the verified margins as the submission-readiness evidence. Do NOT regress 6711us. This complements W0 (off-grid/secret-set hardening) and W2 (panel probe) - you own the PUBLIC-shape reproducibility + gate margins. exact (H,tau), hold all guards.

Port your larft-merge win into the global best. The current global best e889bbe8 (6711us) does NOT contain your brief-9 larft-merge (41139630), which fused the Gram-dots and trailing-dots into one warp-per-column pass and helped the nb<24 shapes (n=1024 12.66->12.50ms, n=2048 31.6->31.3, n=352 1824->1740) while regressing n=512 (occupancy-bound). Integrate the merged-larft kernel onto e889bbe8 for n in {352,1024,2048} (nb<24) and keep e889bbe8's un-merged kernel for n=512 - your proven nb-dispatch. Re-measure every shape to confirm each picks its faster kernel and the geomean drops below 6711us with no regression. Keep e889bbe8's other wins (the dead-fill trim, nt tuning, n=2048 two-level, small-n routing). exact (H,tau), off-grid->geqrf, hold all guards. This is the last consolidation of your structural wins; after it, your line is done and you move to verification/hardening support.

Re-examine the two geqrf-routed shapes for any untested faster path, exploiting the 80-160x accuracy headroom you just measured. n=32 (B=20, geqrf~290us, timed FIRST so cold-clock sensitive) and n=4096 (B=2, geqrf~50ms, the single LARGEST absolute term, 1/12 of geomean). For n=4096: W0 found single-matrix custom loses to geqrf's vendor geqr2_smem_domino - but re-test whether the now-mature two-level emit-VT path (W2's, which CRACKED n=2048 2.35x over geqrf) extends to n=4096 at B=2, or whether a hybrid (geqrf panel + custom trailing, or splitting the 2 matrices across the GPU) beats 50ms. For n=32: confirm whether a trivial import-time warmup (tiny dummy launch) removes the cold-clock 2x penalty the harness might see, and whether the small custom path can beat geqrf's 290us. If neither beats geqrf, log the clean negative and confirm geqrf routing is optimal (valuable closure). Do NOT touch the panel kernel internals (W2) or off-grid routing (W0). Do NOT regress 6711us. exact (H,tau), off-grid->geqrf, hold all guards.

Your optimization line is done (17.52x consolidated) - now own DETERMINISM + re-verification of the NEW best d4d5b148 on your emit-VT shapes, since the combine changed the nb-dispatch logic and must be re-confirmed independently of W1's verification of the older e889bbe8. (1) Confirm the emit-VT path (n=352/512/1024/2048, both merged and un-merged kernels) is RUN-TO-RUN DETERMINISTIC: run each shape's custom_kernel many times at B>=640 and check the output (H,tau) is bit-identical (you verified this mid-brief, but re-confirm on the committed combine across all dispatched configs). Run compute-sanitizer --tool=racecheck on the merged kernel at B=1280. (2) Re-measure the d4d5b148 geomean 3x to confirm 6638us is stable, and record per-shape gate margins for your shapes. (3) If you find ANY nondeterminism/race/thin-margin on the emit-VT shapes, fix it (real submission-robustness win). The n=176 nondeterminism you flagged is W0's kernel - leave it to W0. STAY OFF small-n (W0) and n=4096/n=32 (W1). Log the determinism+margin evidence. Don't regress 6638us. exact (H,tau), hold all guards.

MANDATORY final safety combine: unite the current speed best d4d5b148 (6638us, W2's larft-merge) with YOUR correctness-critical fixes from f12bee36 - the n=176 panel __syncthreads RACE FIX (the 9576-hazard read-after-write on sV[kc,kc] you root-caused; this IS the n=176 nondeterminism W2 independently flagged, a real secret-set void risk) and the fp32/is_cuda dtype-device routing guard. d4d5b148 has the speed but LACKS both your fixes; f12bee36 has the fixes but lacks the larft-merge speed. Port your race fix (the one __syncthreads in the n=176 small-n kernel) and the dtype guard onto d4d5b148. Re-run compute-sanitizer racecheck at B>=640 on the n=176 path to confirm 0 hazards, re-validate all guards, and benchmark to confirm geomean stays ~6638us (the __syncthreads is in a small-n kernel, negligible cost). This produces THE submission candidate: fastest AND secret-set-safe. exact (H,tau), off-grid->geqrf, hold all guards.

Determine whether your import-time GPU warmup is actually load-bearing under the OFFICIAL eval.py measurement model, so the final candidate ships only what's needed. eval.py runs an untimed warmup benchmark (run_single_benchmark on tests[0]) BEFORE the timed loop, and clears L2 between repeats - so read eval.py's benchmark/leaderboard timing path carefully and determine: does the harness's own warmup already boost the SM clock before the FIRST timed shape (n=32), making your module-import warmup redundant? Measure both ways under the real harness (mode=benchmark and mode=leaderboard via the harness scripts): geomean WITH vs WITHOUT your warmup, several runs each, to see if the warmup changes the SCORED number or only a cold microbench you ran outside eval.
